description: Turns a mono signal into a stereo pair by delaying one side, so the ear places the sound toward the side that arrives first

params.text: Sets the delay on the right output, marked 0.025ms to 10ms; the module reads its buffer the wrong way round, so the knob shortens the delay rather than lengthening it

inputs.text: The signal to be spread across the stereo pair

outputs.text: The input, passed straight through with no delay

notes: the delay actually applied is about 93ms at the knob's lowest setting and 83ms at its highest at a 44.1kHz sample rate, and it halves at 96kHz.
the delay changes with Rack's sample rate because the buffer is a fixed 4096 samples whatever the rate.
a delay of that length is past the range where the Haas effect places a sound and is heard as a distinct echo on one side.
the left output is the untouched input, so patching only that jack gives the dry signal.

inputs.0:
continuous · one channel only
